problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨2{t}^{2}-4t,5t-{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=2.$
worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t-4,\,5-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨4(2)-4,\,5-3(2)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨8-4,\,5-12⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-7⟩\end{aligned}
$$
